planner_json.title: Keep a headless OpenCode session alive with the shipped plugin
depends_on: GAW-1 (the real-cli test harness this proof installs the CLI through)

write_prohibited: plugins/pixel-perfect/** except the named module - nothing else in the plugin changes
INSTALL.md - the install under test stays as it is
Any file not listed in WRITE-ALLOWED

seed/real-copy-install.description: A fresh project directory holding the INSTALL.md real copies from this checkout, including the plugin module, with the CLI installed under a temp prefix and a temp HOME

specification.objective: A headless OpenCode run with the shipped plugin installed reaches its command at the pinned version and at the version the newest lookup resolves.
specification.success_state: At both versions, `opencode export` shows 1 user message holding `Invocation input: --platform web-desktop`, and the stream holds no `Unexpected server error`.

requirements.description: GIVEN a fresh project holding the INSTALL.md real copies, including the plugin module, with the CLI installed under a temp prefix and temp HOME WHEN `opencode run --command pixel-perfect/status --format json -- --platform web-desktop` runs with the placeholder key at each version, and `opencode export` reads that session in a keyless child THEN the export holds 1 user message at each of the 2 versions, that message holds `Invocation input: --platform web-desktop`, and the stream holds no `Unexpected server error`
requirements.verification_service: real opencode-ai at the pinned and newest versions, with an empty env and a placeholder key the API rejects
requirements.positive_example: With the module returning {}, opencode run ends in invalid x-api-key and opencode export shows a user message reading Invocation input: --platform web-desktop.
requirements.red: On base the shipped module returns nothing, so opencode run ends in Unexpected server error and opencode export shows 0 user messages at both 1.18.34 and 1.19.5.

scenario.verification_service: real opencode-ai at the pinned and newest versions, with an empty env and a placeholder key the API rejects

would_fail_if: the module still returns nothing, so the session dies before its user message
the test omits the plugin module from the copies, so the shipped module is never loaded

build_proof.range: anything that proves the shipped plugin leaves a headless OpenCode session able to reach its command
examples: the module returning a hooks object

steps: run opencode run --command pixel-perfect/status --format json -- --platform web-desktop with the placeholder key, at each version
run opencode export on that run's session in a keyless child

must_observe: the export holds 1 user message at each of the 2 versions
must_not_observe: an empty messages array in the export
